transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from polishing a display of Golden Snitches*

Good afternoon, and welcome to Quality Quidditch Supplies! What can I help you with today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hello! I bought a broom-servicing kit from your shop recently, but it turns out the handle polish is dried out and the tail-twig clippers are rusted. I was hoping to get a replacement or a refund.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns slightly and leans forward on the counter*

Oh dear, that is unfortunate. When did you purchase this kit, if I may ask? And... *pauses, eyeing you carefully* ...I assume you've already opened it then, to discover these defects?

*picks up a quill, tapping it thoughtfully against the counter*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It was only a few days ago. I bought it last Saturday, to be precise. I understand the need to verify the condition of the items, and I did open the kit to find these issues. I hope that's not a problem.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sets down the quill with a decisive tap and shakes head apologetically*

Ah, well there's the difficulty, I'm afraid. You see, all servicing kits are non-refundable once the seal is broken, Mr. Potter. Store policy, clearly printed on the receipt. 

*crosses arms*

You'll have to take it up with the manufacturer directly — that's a six-week owl exchange minimum, I'm told. Flyte & Barker are based in Aberdeen, dreadfully slow with their correspondence. But there's nothing I can do here at the shop level once the packaging's been tampered with.

*softens tone slightly*

I do sympathize, truly, but rules are rules. We can't have customers opening products and then returning them willy-nilly, you understand.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I get that you have policies in place, but the kit was faulty right out of the box. It's not like I used it and then decided to return it. Can't there be an exception in cases like this? It's not like I can use a dried-out polish or rusted clippers.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sighs and drums fingers on the counter, looking somewhat uncomfortable*

Look, Mr. Potter, I understand your frustration, I really do. But faulty or not, the moment that seal breaks, my hands are tied. The owner is very strict about this — we had a spate of customers last year claiming products were "faulty" after they'd clearly been used, and now there's simply no wiggle room.

*leans in slightly, lowering voice*

Between you and me, Flyte & Barker's quality control has been slipping lately. But that's precisely why we direct customers to them for defects. They're the ones who should be standing behind their product.

*straightens up, speaking more formally again*

I can write you a letter of introduction to send along with your complaint if you'd like — might speed things along a bit. But I cannot process a refund or exchange here. Not my call to make, I'm afraid.

*glances toward the back room nervously, as if the owner might be listening*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: All right, I guess a letter might help. Can you please write it for me? I don't have much experience with this sort of thing, and I want to make sure it's done properly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly relaxes, seeming relieved you're being reasonable*

Of course, of course. That I can certainly do for you.

*reaches under the counter and pulls out a piece of parchment and a proper quill, dipping it in ink*

Let's see now... "To the Customer Service Department at Flyte & Barker Manufacturing, Aberdeen..."

*writes in neat script while speaking aloud*

"This letter serves to introduce Mr. Harry Potter, who purchased one of your standard broom-servicing kits from our establishment on Saturday last. Upon opening, he discovered the handle polish to be dried out and the tail-twig clippers to be rusted, rendering the kit unusable. As a long-standing retailer of your products, we can vouch that Mr. Potter is a valued customer acting in good faith..."

*looks up*

I'll add our shop seal at the bottom — that should carry some weight with them. They'll want you to send the defective kit back with the letter, mind you. Use a sturdy box and pay for the tracking owl service, don't cheap out on a regular post owl or it might never arrive.

*continues writing*

This should at least get their attention, Mr. Potter.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you for your help. I'll follow your advice and send the kit as you suggested. I hope they'll take care of this promptly. Is there anything else I can do while I wait for their response?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*blows gently on the parchment to dry the ink, then rolls it up and hands it to you*

Well, if you need to service your broom in the meantime, I'd recommend bringing it by our workshop in the back. We offer professional cleaning and maintenance services — costs a bit more than doing it yourself, naturally, but at least you'll know it's done right.

*gestures toward a price board on the wall*

Standard service is five Galleons, includes polish, bristle alignment, and a full safety inspection. Takes about three days.

*pauses thoughtfully*

As for dealing with Flyte & Barker... do check your owl every few days. Sometimes they'll send a response asking for more details or photographs of the defects before they approve the exchange. Don't ignore those or you'll be back to square one. And keep your receipt from our shop — they may ask for proof of purchase date.

*taps the rolled parchment you're holding*

That letter should help, but manufacturers can be stubborn. If you haven't heard anything in eight weeks, send a follow-up. Persistence pays off with these things.

Is there anything else you need today, Mr. Potter?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, that's all for now, thanks. I'll bring my broom in for the service. And I'll keep an eye on my owl for any responses from Flyte & Barker. If there are any issues, I'll be sure to follow up. It's a bit of a hassle, but I suppose that's the way it goes sometimes.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods approvingly and slides the letter across the counter*

That's the spirit, Mr. Potter. Sometimes these things just require a bit of patience and persistence. Sorry I couldn't do more for you today, but you're handling it well.

*pulls out an appointment ledger*

Now, if you'd like to book that broom service, I can get you in by... let's see... Thursday afternoon? Just bring the broom round before noon and we'll have it ready for collection Saturday morning.

*smiles more warmly now*

And do let us know if Flyte & Barker gives you any trouble. If they're being particularly difficult after a reasonable time, sometimes a word from the shop owner to their sales representative can... encourage things along, shall we say. We do buy a fair amount of stock from them.

*extends hand for a handshake*

Best of luck with it all. And safe flying in the meantime!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you for your help and the advice. I'll be in on Thursday to drop off my broom. And I'll keep you updated on how things go with Flyte & Barker. If I need to, I'll let you know about the... "encouragement" from the shop owner. I appreciate your support.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shakes your hand firmly*

Excellent, Mr. Potter. We'll take good care of your broom, don't you worry. And yes, do keep us informed — we like to know when our suppliers aren't living up to standards.

*makes a note in the ledger*

Thursday before noon, then. Just ask for me — name's Aldric, by the way — and I'll make sure it goes straight to our best technician.

*waves as you turn to leave*

Good day to you, and hopefully Flyte & Barker will sort you out quickly. Though between us, I wouldn't hold my breath!

*returns to polishing the Snitches with a slight smile*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Goodbye, Aldric. Thanks again for your time and assistance. I'll see you on Thursday.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the Snitches with a friendly nod*

Goodbye, Mr. Potter. See you Thursday!

*returns focus to polishing, humming quietly as you head toward the door*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *exits the shop, feeling a bit better about the situation now that there's a plan in place*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches you leave through the shop window, then mutters to himself while returning the polishing cloth to its proper place*

Nice lad, that one. Shame about Flyte & Barker's shoddy products lately...

*shakes head and turns attention back to arranging the Snitch display, waiting for the next customer*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *makes his way back home, reflecting on the day's events and what he needs to do next*

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry accepts the clerk's alternative solutions (letter, broom service) without resistance, showing moderate flexibility but no particular creativity or exploration of novel approaches.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry precisely recalls the purchase date ('last Saturday'), carefully follows instructions about tracking and receipts, and commits to follow-up actions, demonstrating organized and responsible behavior.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry's interactions are polite but reserved, focused on the transactional task at hand with minimal social elaboration or enthusiasm beyond what's necessary.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Despite initial frustration, Harry accepts store policy without argument, thanks the clerk multiple times, and cooperates fully: 'All right, I guess a letter might help' shows accommodation.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry remains calm throughout the refusal, accepts the hassle with mild resignation ('I suppose that's the way it goes sometimes'), showing emotional stability under disappointment.
